item.title: The Modular Building Company Quietly Riding the AI Boom
item.description: McGrath RentCorp rents modular buildings and portable storage to schools and contractors — not exactly a headline-grabbing business. But buried inside its earnings is a test-equipment segment growing double digits on data center and AI infrastructure demand, a 33-year dividend growth streak, and a stock trading well below analysts' fair value estimate. Alex and Jordan dig into why nobody's talking about this one.

item.title: The Workers' Comp Company That Bought Back 70% of Itself
item.description: Everyone's ignoring CorVel Corporation, a debt-free, thirty-year compounder in the unglamorous world of workers' comp claims management and medical bill repricing. We dig into why revenue growth just reaccelerated to 11%, why the stock is still down nearly 50% over the past year, and why almost nobody is talking about it.

item.title: The Fed Finally Pulls the Trigger: Rate Hikes Are Back
item.description: The Fed hikes rates for the first time since 2023, Treasury yields punch through levels not seen since 2007, and Wall Street spends the week trying to figure out if this is a one-and-done move or the start of something longer. Alex and Jordan break down the FOMC decision, a wild divergence between the Dow and the Nasdaq, Netflix's ugly downgrade, and why small-cap stocks are having a moment nobody's talking about.
